title: See link property types in references

intentCoverage.report:
Dough Intent Coverage — SEED-131 "See link property types in references" (plan 100), revision fcd05a8199d1c5894e8b6010198fea84283ea127

Verdict: Caught. The claim covers only the References path that runs through `NoteRealmService.build`.

Promise probed: "No new restriction: which references appear, their order, the caps and the sampling stay as they are", for the web References section. The behavior checked: a referrer note gets one References entry, even when it has several references that resolve to the same target.

Fault: In `AuthoredNoteReferenceInboundFacade.distinctInboundReferencesForViewer`, the final loop builds one `InboundReference` for each resolved candidate row (loops over `referrerIdByRowId.values()`) instead of one for each referrer (`referrersInOrder`). Ascending order still holds; only merging of duplicate referrers is broken. No fixtures or assertions changed.

Baseline (scratch worktree at the selected revision, own test database): `*AuthoredNoteReferenceInboundFacadeTest` 4 of 4 passed; `*NoteRealmServiceTest` 10 tests plus 4 in nested `ReferencePropertyTypes`, all passed.

With the fault (`*NoteRealmServiceTest`): 14 ran, 1 failed — `NoteRealmServiceTest.references_dedupe_multiple_authored_references_for_same_carrier_note` (content `"[[Focal]] and [[Focal|again]]"`, `assertThat(noteRealmService.build(focal, user).getReferences(), hasSize(1))`) failed with "collection size was <2>", the same note listed twice on the intended path. Not one of the assertions rewritten through `NoteRealmReferences.referrerIds`. `ReferencePropertyTypes.lists_each_distinct_type_once_in_authored_order` also asserts `hasSize(1)` but passed (inferred: its repeated identical link gives one resolved row). The faulted code was not run against `AuthoredNoteReferenceInboundFacadeTest`; by reading, each setup has one reference per referring note.

Restoration: file reverted; scratch `git status` clean at fcd05a8199; `*NoteRealmServiceTest` rerun passed 10 + 4; scratch worktree removed. Live workspace never edited.

Next proof action: none needed for the duplicate-referrer case on this path. Optional: a separate probe breaking ascending order would confirm the facade-level order test catches it.

Cost: test runtime about 5m44s (baseline facade 1m51s, baseline realm 1m01s, faulted realm 1m34s, restored realm 1m18s); human and agent effort unavailable; invocation-to-report 461555 ms (about 7m42s).

Wrap-up disposition: fcd05a8199d1c5894e8b6010198fea84283ea127 — Caught — no follow-up.
